summary: Deep test of the limit removal (100 MB per PDF only, no page cap, no mock cap) and the new scale architecture. Backend used the real FastAPI app via ASGITransport with real JWT, in disposable DBs tejas_isolated_book170_<hex>; all were dropped. The real sealed PDF worker subprocess was used. Storage transport and AI were MOCKED. Results: new suite tests/book_scale_iso171.py 54/57 (2 HIGH/CRITICAL root causes). Adapted 170 regression: main 105/105, rules 40/41 (the one failure is the old '51 mocks rejected' assertion; 51 mocks now publish, as intended, and the test is updated), ext 60/60. What works: exactly 100 MiB is accepted at the API and as a real file (200 parts end to end), 100 MiB+1 gets 422, and listing limits are {bytes:104857600,pages:null,mocks:null}. A 1,501-page / 150-mock book reads in 75 steps of 20 pages (average 0.35s, max step 4.7s, 127s total, ~215 MB RSS). Every page persisted with no 1000-page error. All 150 mocks (including 3-digit labels) were detected in book order and published at most 5 per step, each with its own questions, correct keys and mock_number. Page-list pagination works at p41 (1001-1025) and p61 (1501). Series detail and list show all 150. Map-range over 1300 pages takes 2.8s. Page repair on page 1393 re-clips text from the source. AI allowance accepts pages 1200/1501 and rejects 1502 with 422. Large files: 91 MiB/183 parts and exactly 100 MiB/200 parts with incompressible images. Interrupted after 150 parts, GET showed all 150 received parts, resume sent only the missing ones, a duplicate identical part was idempotent, parts were deleted after the original was stored byte-exact, and 20 mocks published in ~26s (max step 5.7s, maxrss ~580 MB). Cache: original() returns the verified disk path; a deleted cache is re-downloaded and verified; corrupted storage bytes put the book in 'failed' with an integrity message, 0 sets, and retry resumes. Concurrent page-image and preview-crop requests during worker runs and on a cold cache all returned 200. An injected lease 409 during publication held no mock, and retry published all mocks. A batch that crashes falls back per page and only that page gets the issue. Frontend (Playwright on preview, /api/** forwarded to an isolated bridge on 127.0.0.1:8770): a real browser chunked upload of a 54.7 MB / 110-part PDF paused after 41 parts and resumed with 69 parts and 0 overlap, then processed to 12 published mocks. Owner detail of a 1,141-page / 60-mock book renders all 60 mocks with pagination 4/46. Series page lists all 60 at both 1920x800 and 390x844 with no overflow. Client-side >100MB rejection fires with no API call. Two real defects remain (see action_items).

critical.issue: ENDLESS JOB LOOP: a book uploaded with auto_publish=false that has more than 5 ready mocks never finishes. publish_ready() returns immediately when auto_publish is false, but publish_batch still does published+=1 for each ready mock and returns True after 5. step() then sets more=True, state stays 'matching' and it re-enqueues forever: a full rebuild over all pages and mocks every step, burning CPU and the job lane. Reproduced: 1,501 pages / 150 mocks with auto_publish false is still 'matching' with message 'Publishing clean mocks in batches: 0 of 150 released so far.' after 110 steps, with a new job queued every step (>250 jobs in a few minutes). Older suites missed this because their manual books had 5 or fewer ready mocks. Fix: return False early in publish_batch when book.paused or not book.payload['auto_publish'], and count only mocks actually published or held.

The ROLE heading regex still uses (?:test|mock|paper)\s*(?:no\.?\s*)?\d{1,2}, while MOCK was widened to \d{1,3}. So labelled key or solution headings for mocks 100 and above ('Answer Key - Mock Test 100', 'Solutions for Mock Test 120') are not recognised as role switches. The key page is then read as question pages and the mock is held with 'Q1: confirm response type, options and continuation.' This fails closed, but blocks the new >99-mock feature for books that label their key sections. Reproduced: mocks 9/99/100/101 with labelled key headings give 9 and 99 published, 100 and 101 held; with plain 'Answer Key' all 4 publish. Verified that changing \d{1,2} to \d{1,3} in ROLE makes these headings match.

minor.issue: The cache is pruned to the 6 newest originals, up to ~600 MB in /tmp. With 7+ books processing at once, one worker can unlink a cached file another is about to stat/link in book_pdf.run(). That raises FileNotFoundError, which is not a ValueError, so the book fails with 'Processing interrupted'. It recovers on retry. Not reproduced under test load; the risk was found in code review.

The 64 MB in-process ByteCache means integrity of storage bytes is only re-checked after a process restart or cache eviction. This is fine, but note it for future storage-corruption tests: clear tejas_storage._source_cache.

issues: Rejecting a 100 MiB+1 file still shows '0.0 / 100.0 MB received' because of rounding next to the 'Choose a PDF within 100 MB.' error, which is slightly confusing. Hide the progress bar when validation fails.

Each mock's 'instructions:' page chips list every question page, because the 'Physics' subject header on each question page is stored as an instructions region. For long mocks this makes a very long chip row. Cosmetic.

action_items: CRITICAL: fix the endless re-enqueue for auto_publish=false books with more than 5 ready mocks in book_worker.publish_batch (return False when not auto_publish or paused; increment only on a real publish or hold). Then retest: tests/book_scale_iso171.py pages, check 'auto_publish=False book processing TERMINATES'.

HIGH: widen the ROLE regex mock number in book_reader.py from \d{1,2} to \d{1,3} so 'Answer Key - Mock Test 100' and 'Solutions for Mock Test 120' switch the role. Retest: tests/book_scale_iso171.py key3.
Optional: make book_pdf.run robust to a cache file vanishing (re-resolve through cached() or catch OSError as a retryable ValueError); hide the upload progress bar on client-side validation errors.
critical_code_review_comments: book_worker.publish_batch counts skipped (non-auto) mocks as work done, which causes the loop above.
book_reader ROLE and MOCK regexes disagree on digit width (1-2 vs 1-3).
step() runs rebuild() over all pages and mocks on every matching step. At 1,500 pages / 150 mocks a step is ~4.7s, which is acceptable but grows linearly per step. Consider incremental rebuild.
receive() joins all parts in memory (~100 MB) on top of loading the part documents: peak RSS ~580 MB for a 100 MiB book. Acceptable, but streaming the parts to a temp file would halve it.
Test harness note: inspect() now takes a path, not bytes. The 170 limits() test was adapted to write files.

In Playwright, route **/api/** to 127.0.0.1:8770 with cookies added via url=BASE. Avoid f-strings in screenshot paths with the browser tool. Afterwards, delete /tmp/jeelive-book-originals/*.pdf.
rca of the issue: 1) Endless loop: publish_ready early-returns when auto_publish is false, but publish_batch increments published per ready mock and returns True after MOCKS_PER_STEP, so step() always re-enqueues. Repro: upload any book with more than 5 clean mocks and auto_publish=false. Mitigation: guard in publish_batch. 2) Labelled 3-digit key headings: ROLE uses \d{1,2}, so ROLE.fullmatch('Answer Key - Mock Test 100') is False and role context stays 'question'. Repro: tests/book_scale_iso171.py key3. Mitigation: \d{1,3}.
